backlog.title: Field-Level Type Overrides (§6.4)
backlog.description: Implement PRD §6.4: Field-Level Overrides for Type-Level Levers. This adds six optional override fields to FieldConfig (defaultValue, debounce, parser, formatter, valueField, getSubmitField) so a single field instance can override its input TYPE's behavior without affecting other fields of the same type. The codebase is otherwise mature — this is the sole remaining unimplemented PRD feature. All six levers share one precedence rule via a single core helper (resolveFieldOverType): the field-level value wins over the type-level value when !== undefined (so null/false/0/"" are meaningful). Validator composes (already implemented); these six override.

subtasks.title: Add field-level override fields to FieldConfig type
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: FieldConfig is in `packages/core/src/types/config.ts` (interface FieldConfig, ~line 42-92). It currently does NOT have defaultValue, debounce, parser, formatter, valueField, or getSubmitField. These exist ONLY on InputConfig (same file). The PRD §6.4 requires FieldConfig to mirror them as per-instance overrides. The PRD §6.4.5 states `undefined` = 'not specified' and all other values (null, false, 0, "") are meaningful overrides.
2. INPUT: The existing `FieldConfig` interface at `packages/core/src/types/config.ts`.
3. LOGIC: Add six optional fields to FieldConfig, placed after `recordKey` and before `rules` (matching PRD §3.2 FieldConfig layout):
  - `defaultValue?: unknown` — Per-instance default; overrides type default (§6.4.1). JSDoc: 'Per-instance default value. Overrides the input type\'s defaultValue; superseded by record/defaultValues prop. Honored when !== undefined, so null/false/0/"" are meaningful. See §6.4.1, §13.1.'
  - `debounce?: number | false` — Per-instance debounce (§6.4.2). JSDoc: 'Per-instance auto-save debounce. Overrides the input type\'s debounce; falls back to Form-level debounce prop (default 1000). false = submit immediately. See §6.4.2.'
  - `parser?: string | ((value: unknown) => unknown)` — Per-instance parser (§6.4.3). JSDoc: 'Per-instance value transform (input→form). Overrides the input type\'s parser. String = named parser; function = inline. See §6.4.3.'
  - `formatter?: string | ((value: unknown) => unknown)` — Per-instance formatter (§6.4.3). JSDoc: 'Per-instance value transform (form→display). Overrides the input type\'s formatter. String = named formatter; function = inline. See §6.4.3.'
  - `valueField?: string` — Per-instance submit value extraction (§6.4.4). JSDoc: 'Submit-side value extraction from complex objects. Overrides the input type\'s valueField. See §6.4.4.'
  - `getSubmitField?: (fieldName: string) => string` — Per-instance submit key mapping (§6.4.4). JSDoc: 'Submit-side field name transformation. Overrides the input type\'s getSubmitField. See §6.4.4.'
  IMPORTANT: parser/formatter use `(value: unknown) => unknown` (NOT TValue-generic) because FieldConfig is not generic over TValue (PRD §6.4.3). The existing InputConfig already has the same fields at lines ~80-100 of config.ts — copy their shapes.
4. OUTPUT: Updated `FieldConfig` interface with the six new optional fields. Since `ReactFieldConfig extends Omit<FieldConfig, 'rules'>`, these fields propagate to the React overlay automatically (no structural change to overlays.ts).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on each new field in config.ts references §6.4 sub-sections. This rides WITH the work — do NOT create a separate docs subtask.

subtasks.title: Wire effective parser/formatter via resolveFieldOverType in useField
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: `packages/react/src/hooks/useField.tsx` has two transform sites. (a) `handleChange` (parse): calls `parse(newValue, inputConfig.parser, providerConfig.parsers)` — this is a `useCallback` (~line 200). (b) Controller render callback (format): calls `format(field.value, inputConfig.formatter, providerConfig.formatters)` — this is inside the `Controller` render prop (~line 310). Both currently use `inputConfig.parser`/`inputConfig.formatter` directly. The `fieldConfig` variable (from `config[name] ?? {}`) is in scope at both sites. The `parse`/`format` functions are imported from `@formality-ui/core`. The PRD §5.3.5 says 'Effective spec (§6.4.3). The parser/formatter applied below is the effective one — fieldConfig.parser ?? inputConfig.parser.' The existing `packages/react/src/__tests__/useField.test.tsx` covers useField behavior.
2. INPUT: `resolveFieldOverType` from P1.M1.T1.S2; updated `FieldConfig` with `parser?` and `formatter?` from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC:
  (a) Import `resolveFieldOverType` from `@formality-ui/core` at the top of useField.tsx.
  (b) Compute effective parser/formatter in a `useMemo` (or inline if simpler):
  ```typescript
  const effectiveParser = useMemo(
    () => resolveFieldOverType(fieldConfig.parser, inputConfig.parser),
    [fieldConfig.parser, inputConfig.parser],
  );
  const effectiveFormatter = useMemo(
    () => resolveFieldOverType(fieldConfig.formatter, inputConfig.formatter),
    [fieldConfig.formatter, inputConfig.formatter],
  );
  ```
  (c) In `handleChange`: replace `inputConfig.parser` with `effectiveParser`.
  (d) In Controller render callback: replace `inputConfig.formatter` with `effectiveFormatter`.
  (e) Add `effectiveParser`/`effectiveFormatter` to the respective `useCallback`/`useMemo` dependency arrays.
4. OUTPUT: `useField` applies the field-level parser/formatter when set, falling back to the type-level. Named registries (`providerConfig.parsers`/`.formatters`) stay global and unchanged.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update JSDoc on `InputConfig.parser` and `InputConfig.formatter` in `packages/core/src/types/config.ts` to mention the three-tier precedence (field → type → none). The existing InputConfig.parser/formatter JSDoc (~line 92-100) should add: 'Per-field override via FieldConfig.parser/formatter (§6.4.3); field wins when !== undefined.' This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Wire field-level debounce via resolveFieldOverType in changeField
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: `packages/react/src/components/Form.tsx` has `changeField` as a `useCallback` (~line 155-185). It currently resolves `const fieldDebounce = inputConfig?.debounce;` and branches: false→executeAutoSaveRef, number→getOrCreateDebouncedRef, undefined→debouncedSubmitRef. The `config` variable (the form's FormFieldsConfig) is in scope (it's a prop). So `config[name]?.debounce` gives the field-level debounce. The PRD §6.4.2 precedence is: fieldConfig.debounce → inputConfig.debounce → Form-level debounce prop (default 1000). The existing `packages/react/src/__tests__/autosave-field-debounce.test.tsx` covers InputConfig.debounce; new tests should cover FieldConfig.debounce overriding it. The `changeField` function is exposed via FormContextValue and called from useField's handleChange as `changeField(name, parsedValue, inputConfig)`.
2. INPUT: `resolveFieldOverType` from P1.M1.T1.S2; updated `FieldConfig` with `debounce?` from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC:
  (a) Import `resolveFieldOverType` from `@formality-ui/core` in Form.tsx (it already imports from core).
  (b) In `changeField`, replace:
  ```typescript
  const fieldDebounce = inputConfig?.debounce;
  ```
  With:
  ```typescript
  const fieldConfig = config[name];
  const fieldDebounce = resolveFieldOverType(
    fieldConfig?.debounce,
    inputConfig?.debounce,
  );
  ```
  The existing branching logic (false→immediate, number→per-field timer, undefined→Form-level) remains unchanged — `resolveFieldOverType` returns the field-level value when set, otherwise the type-level, otherwise undefined (which falls through to the Form-level debounce).
  (c) Add `config` to the `changeField` `useCallback` dependency array if not already present.
4. OUTPUT: `changeField` honors `fieldConfig.debounce` when !== undefined, falling back to `inputConfig.debounce`, then to the Form-level `debounce` prop. The three-tier debounce precedence from §6.4.2 is enforced.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update `InputConfig.debounce` JSDoc in `packages/core/src/types/config.ts` to add the three-tier precedence statement: 'Three-tier precedence (§6.4.2): a field-level FieldConfig.debounce wins when set; otherwise this type-level value; otherwise the Form-level debounce prop (default 1000). All three share the single field-over-type rule from §6.4.0.' The existing JSDoc (~line 70-80) already has a two-tier statement — extend it to three tiers. This rides WITH the work.
